### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b89b33978b9bd68a71a9e30755edbc8ed80fa5c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1458df6aded1a1f79f6e9e3f185cc0e911247df2` — the merge of head `c6a4f1aae6420258b00cc928781622af7fb176b3` into base `0b89b33978b9bd68a71a9e30755edbc8ed80fa5c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1458df6aded1a1f79f6e9e3f185cc0e911247df2 && git checkout 1458df6aded1a1f79f6e9e3f185cc0e911247df2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0b89b33978b9bd68a71a9e30755edbc8ed80fa5c c6a4f1aae6420258b00cc928781622af7fb176b3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0b89b33978b9bd68a71a9e30755edbc8ed80fa5c && git merge --no-ff c6a4f1aae6420258b00cc928781622af7fb176b3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b89b33978b9bd68a71a9e30755edbc8ed80fa5c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c6a4f1aae6420258b00cc928781622af7fb176b3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.stored-row-holder-lists-pair-member.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts (`holdsNameForExactRead`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts (the scoped list's pair added-member rule)

Inputs read: card #33131 body and all 11 comments (rulings 6868829990 and the carried note 6870666736 included), PR #33220 body and file list, the net diff against `main` at this head (6 files, +163 / -9), and the 67 check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read in the live tree, never reviewed: `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (`packageScopedHoldersOf`, `overlaySlotBinding`, `overlayRowBinding`, `pairRowBinding`, `getPackageScopedItem`), `protocol-exact-qualifier.ts` (`admitExactQualifier`, `exactQualifierItem`, `pairRowOnAddress`, `pairMemberWithheldAt`), `protocol-write-gates.ts` (`shipsBundleName`, `baseServesBundleMember`), `protocol-environment-rows.ts` (`baseAddressServesMember`), `protocol-overlay-merge.ts` (`mergePackageAwareOverlay`), `protocol-artifact-lookup.ts` (`shippingPackagesOf`), `metadata-core` `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS`, `objectql` `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES`. The remainder of the diff (the test file, the two changesets) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of the scoped list (`GET /api/v1/meta/TYPE?package=ID`) and of the execution list a send reads: widened by one row class. Right.** The rule at `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts` L713-731 un-withholds an unseated pair row when `(shipsBundleName OR holdsNameForExactRead) AND baseServesBundleMember AND NOT pairMemberWithheldAt`. Only the first conjunct gained an alternative; the two withholding conjuncts are untouched. Nothing a list served before is removed.
- **No list answer exceeds the exact read. Right.** The third conjunct calls `pairRowOnAddress` with the same `holders` argument (`packageScopedHoldersOf(type, name)`, served holders, no caller) and the same registry binding the exact read's judge (`exactQualifierItem`) passes; the list passes bases `[X]`, the exact read `[X, ...registryHolders]`, so the list is never the wider of the two. The new first conjunct (`X` in the served holders, no caller) is a subset of the exact read's admission (`packageScopedHoldersOf(type, name, X, includeDisabledPackages)` includes `X`).
- **Exact read: unchanged. Right.** No hunk touches `admitExactQualifier`, `exactQualifierItem` or `pairRowOnAddress`; `holdsNameForExactRead` is a new export with one caller.
- **Public surface: one new exported function from an internal module (`protocol-exact-qualifier.ts`), no schema key, no stored-row shape. Right**, and the entry says so (no tombstone, no D2 conversion).
- **Type reach: `email_template` alone.** `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` has that one key and it is in `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES`, so the `readsByPackage` gate inside `holdsNameForExactRead` is true for every type the rule runs on today. It fails closed (returns false, list as on `main`) for a registry without the exact qualifier's reads or a future bundled type not read by package, matching `pairMemberWithheldAt` beside it.
- **Item 4: no accept-set change. Right**, per ruling 6868829990 (option A); the diff adds a pin only.
- **Gate verdicts (check-runs on this head):** 67 runs, every one `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending. Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, the Lint and Type Check families, Test Core 1-8/8, Test UI 1-16/16 and Dogfood Regression Gate are green.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` **minor**, `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, ADR-0087 marker `registered stored-row-holder-lists-pair-member`: matches what the diff publishes (a served-answer change on a read door, no key, no export removed) and the precedent of the sibling PR #33189 on this card. Accepted.
- `@objectstack/spec` **patch**, `Metadata-protocol: none`: the entry adds text to the upgrade guide and no key or export. Accepted; same shape as #33189's entry changeset.
- Clause-②: no — correct. The change only adds a row to two lists; nothing that was served is refused and no declared capability is taken away, so it is not a narrowing. The PR body and both changesets carry the same line.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation "item 4 ships as a pin only": answered by ruling 6868829990 (maintainer, option A) on the card. Accepted.
- Deviation "Refs, not Fixes": answered by the seat's carried note 6870666736 (the both-overridden registry face stays on the card). Accepted; the card must stay open after this lands.
- Deviation "first pr_create relay run failed, nothing written": process only, no tree effect. Accepted.
- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- `out_of_scope_findings` (a bare read of a `doc` name two namespaces ship serves the first-registered holder's item, "noted, not filed"): **escalated to the seat.** It is a registration-order pick on a by-name read, the red-line-2 family, measured identical on `main`. It is outside this PR, but "noted, not filed" leaves it with no owner; it needs a triage card or a line on this one.
- `security_findings`: none reported; none found in the reviewed files.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.stored-row-holder-lists-pair-member.ts` (hits).** Holds against the code and the scenario it is accepted against (card item 5, comment 6865563363's measurement, re-measured in the PR as holders `[suitex, suite.custom]`).
- `surface` names the right doors (scoped list, execution list), the right type class, and the right trigger (name held only through the package's own stored row; undeclared row of another member in the App's pair). Sentence by sentence it matches L713-731.
- `replacement` ("nothing to rewrite"; a row meant for another package declares it) agrees with `pairRowOnAddress`'s first arm (a declared base is that base's member only).
- `reason` states the FROM accurately: the list asked `shipsBundleName` (code artifacts, via `shippedArtifactsOf`) while the exact read's judge counted `packageScopedHoldersOf`, which adds the package a bare-slot entry binds to.
- `acceptanceCriteria`: the two exclusions (second holder; row declaring another package) are the two withholding checks left untouched, and both are pinned as CONTROLs in both orders.
- No `relevance` question: correct, a stack definition cannot state a runtime stored row.

**`protocol-exact-qualifier.ts` `holdsNameForExactRead` and its call site.** Attempts to break it, each read against the live tree:
1. *Disabled holder X.* `packageScopedHoldersOf` with no caller drops a disabled package, so the new conjunct is false and X's list is as on `main`; the exact read at a disabled X is the withheld 404. No widening.
2. *Second holder Y disabled.* Served holders are `[X]`; the list now carries the row and the exact read serves it through the same `pairRowOnAddress` call over the same served holders (#32183, ruling R4-A). They agree.
3. *Composite slot.* `shipsBundleName` was already true; the new disjunct adds nothing. Pinned as the existing CONTROL.
4. *Code artifact AND a stored row.* Same as 3; where X ships the member itself, `baseServesBundleMember` still answers false for the pair's undeclared row (`baseAddressServesMember`), unchanged.
5. *X holds the row's own member through a second stored row of its own.* That slot has a real contribution from X, so `mergePackageAwareOverlay` serves X's own row and the pair row is never recorded in `unseated`; the new rule cannot reach it. No duplicate member in the list.
6. *`readsByPackage` false.* The function returns false; the list is as on `main`. Today no such bundled type exists (see ①).
7. *The pair package itself as a holder.* In item 5's state the pair is in the served holders (its row binds to itself when no composite slot pairs it). Scoped to the pair, its rows are the list's own placed rows, not stand-ins, so the rule does not run on them; in the judge, `isPairOf(PAIR, PAIR)` is no owner. No effect.
8. *Two stored-row holders in one App, or a code holder beside X.* `pairMemberOwners` counts both, `pairRowOnAddress` refuses, the row stays withheld. Pinned (second-holder CONTROL).

No must-fix and no should-fix found.

Findings:
- **nit (N1), read-derived, not measured.** `acceptanceCriteria` says the lists carry the member "exactly when" the exact read serves it. One corner is narrower: X's stored-row holding is a bundle ADDITION to a holder D in X's dependency closure and outside X's App. `packageScopedHoldersOf` with no caller drops X, so `holdsNameForExactRead` is false and the list leaves the pair row out, while the exact read admits X (its admission counts the named package's own holding) and `pairRowOnAddress` serves the row (no holder pairs it). The list is the narrower side, it is the answer `main` gives, and by the registry's own vocabulary an addition "holds no name", so the entry's wording survives; the same disagreement class the card closes remains in that corner. Leave the head as it is; carry it on the card (it stays open) for a measurement.
- **nit (N2).** The jsdoc of `holdsNameForExactRead` says "as the exact read counts it". The exact read counts twice: its admission asks with the named package as caller and disabled holders included, its judge asks the served holders with no caller. The function adopts the judge's count, which is the safe one (cases 1 and N1). The sentence is true of the judge only. No effect on correctness; fold into any later touch of the file.

Outside ④ (lane seat's ACCEPT, noted for it only): the "pair row declares Y" CONTROL asserts X's read is `not 'pair de-DE'` without registering Y as a holder, so it pins the declared-base arm alone; it is green and sufficient for that arm.
